evidence.excerpt: A coupled simulation workflow was developed to map condensation risk on internal surfaces of wall-mounted outdoor plastic housings under winter conditions. A three-dimensional steady-state CFD model computed the internal temperature distribution accounting for natural convection and wall conduction; the resulting surface temperature field was then passed as a boundary condition to a vapour diffusion model that predicted local relative humidity and dew-point margin at each surface node. A 6-litre ABS housing with a 20 W internal heat source was simulated at external temperatures of −10 °C, 0 °C, and 10 °C at 90 % external relative humidity with a seal permeance of 3.5 × 10⁻¹² kg/(m²·s·Pa). At −10 °C, 14 % of the internal wall area showed a negative dew-point margin; this reduced to 3 % at 0 °C and to zero at 10 °C. A redesign placing the heat source at the geometric bottom of the housing eliminated the negative-margin area at −10 °C. The workflow is implemented in open-source tools and requires less than 4 hours of computation time on a workstation.
